>
> Dear Bioconductor core team,
>
> I maintain BamScale, which was accepted on 4 May 2026
> (Bioconductor/Contributions issue #4128) and is currently in the 3.24 devel
> nightly builds at version 0.99.14. The package has never been part of a
> Bioconductor release.
>
> I would like to rename it to BamScaleR before the 3.24 release. The reason
> is [REASON, e.g. to avoid confusion with the existing BAMscale command-line
> tool from NCBI (github.com/ncbi/BAMscale), which does something
> different]. I have checked that BamScaleR does not exist on CRAN or in
> Bioconductor (BiocManager::install("BamScaleR") fails and the name is
> absent from the 3.24 manifest).
>
> I am aware that the guidelines describe renaming as deprecating the old
> package and resubmitting the new one for review. Since BamScale has not
> been in any release, there are no users to protect with a deprecation
> cycle. I noticed the same situation was handled by renaming the repository
> directly for SingleRBookWrapper -> SingleRBook (Contributions #1609) and
> scTypeR -> scClassifR (Contributions #1798), and I hope the same is
> possible here.
>
> Concretely, could you:
>
>   1. rename packages/BamScale to packages/BamScaleR on
> git.bioconductor.org,
>   2. update the entry in the 3.24 software manifest,
>   3. update the push-access configuration so my SSH key maps to the new
> repository,
>   4. let me know whether I should push the renamed DESCRIPTION before or
> after
>      your change.
>
> On my side I will rename the GitHub repository (cparsania/BamScale ->
> cparsania/BamScaleR), change the Package field and all internal references
> (useDynLib, native routine registration, vignette, documentation, URLs),
> bump to  0.99.15, and push to the renamed upstream to trigger a build. The
> version will stay in the 0.99.x pre-release series.
>
> I would like to complete this well before the release branch for 3.24 is
> created, so the renamed package gets clean nightly builds first. If you
> would rather I go through the deprecate-and-resubmit route via
> BiocContributions instead, I will do that, though I would hope to avoid
> missing the 3.24 release.
>
> Thank you very much for your help.
>
> Best regards,
> Dr. Chirag Parsania

We are moving off that server to a more performant and cloud-based infrastructure; the change was necessitated by increasing and abrupt unsustainable traffic to the old infrastructure. Since late September, the site has been served from on entirely new infrastructure and rebuilt from the same package metadata (with the caveat that we are also in parallel integrating r-universe).

In the move to new infrastructure, the intent was to keep the package pages as close as possible to the originals. The new website html generation process also required update, so while the website looks very similar, it is built from scratch to be faster and more flexible. The first version changed more than it should have, and that's on me.

As of today, the pages are much closer to the old layout again:

- Same section order: Installation, Documentation, Details (with "See More"), Package Archives.
- "In Bioconductor since" uses the same source as before, so it agrees with the badge again (limma: BioC 1.6 or earlier, > 21.5 years).
- The duplicate download-rank row is gone.
- The Documentation links that led back to the same page are fixed. That was a bug in the tool that builds the pages, not intended behaviour.
- NEWS, the installation pointer and the unlinked base packages (splines ships with R) are as they were on the old pages.
- The code browser link returns once code.bioconductor.org's certificate problem is fixed. I have testing that runs each day that checks this.

Going forward, the package pages should stay close to what you were used to. The new website can generate PR review sites, so we can have live previews of substantial changes.

If you want the longer story, the plan and current status are at https://seandavi.github.io/bioc-infrastructure/ ("How bioconductor.org works" and the roadmap are the best starting points). If anything else is missing or wrong, reply here or file a report at https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues. Best,
Sean

messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas,

Thanks for reporting this. Our package pages currently take versions and files from the existing build system, but they take vignette lists from r-universe; this is a weird transition state. When r-universe can't build a package's vignettes, the list comes up empty, even though the vignette is on bioconductor.org. We'll make the pages read vignettes from the same place as everything else. It affects a couple of hundred packages, tracked here:

https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/108

For drugTargetInteractions there's a real issue underneath. The r-universe build of 1.21.14 fails while building the vignette:

  Quitting from drugTargetInteractions.Rmd:564-570 [gtopdb_build]
  Error in `.util_download()`: bfcadd() failed

buildGtoPdbDb() downloads https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/services/interactions, and GtoPdb now requires an API key for its web services. Every /services/ endpoint returns 401 "API key is missing". The HGNC mapping file is still public.

The Bioconductor build still shows the vignette as OK, most likely because the build machines keep BiocFileCache between runs, so buildGtoPdbDb(rerun = FALSE) finds a cached copy and never downloads. r-universe starts from an empty cache every time, so it hits the 401. I'd expect the Bioconductor build to fail too once that cache is refreshed. Build machines won't have an API key, so the vignette probably needs to run without that download or needs an API key: for example a small bundled extract, or skipping the chunk when the download fails.

Separately, BiocCheck on r-universe reports one error: "At least 80% of man pages documenting exported objects must have runnable examples." The daily Bioconductor build doesn't run BiocCheck, so you won't have seen it there.

Full logs, while GitHub keeps them:

https://github.com/r-universe/bioc/actions/runs/35435072146

On the layout: I agree the landing pages matter for exactly the reasons you give. For now we're deliberately keeping them close to the old pages, but I have played with some new layouts such as https://bioconductor.org/next/bioc-release/package/drugTargetInteractions.html. Any redesign, dashboard-style or otherwise, needs proper community review first, and wasn?t something that we wanted as a side effect of the migration. I've recorded your suggestion so it's part of that discussion:
https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/109

Thanks again,
Sean

> place as everything else. It affects a couple of hundred packages, tracked

>
> For drugTargetInteractions there's a real issue underneath. The r-universe
> build of 1.21.14 fails while building the vignette:
>
>   Quitting from drugTargetInteractions.Rmd:564-570 [gtopdb_build]
>   Error in `.util_download()`: bfcadd() failed
>
> buildGtoPdbDb() downloads
> https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/services/interactions, and GtoPdb now
> requires an API key for its web services. Every /services/ endpoint returns
> 401 "API key is missing". The HGNC mapping file is still public.
>
> The Bioconductor build still shows the vignette as OK, most likely because
> the build machines keep BiocFileCache between runs, so buildGtoPdbDb(rerun
> = FALSE) finds a cached copy and never downloads. r-universe starts from an
> empty cache every time, so it hits the 401. I'd expect the Bioconductor
> build to fail too once that cache is refreshed. Build machines won't have
> an API key, so the vignette probably needs to run without that download or
> needs an API key: for example a small bundled extract, or skipping the
> chunk when the download fails.
>
> Separately, BiocCheck on r-universe reports one error: "At least 80% of
> man pages documenting exported objects must have runnable examples." The
> daily Bioconductor build doesn't run BiocCheck, so you won't have seen it
> there.
>
> Full logs, while GitHub keeps them:
>
> https://github.com/r-universe/bioc/actions/runs/35435072146
>

> you give. For now we're deliberately keeping them close to the old pages,
> but I have played with some new layouts such as
> https://bioconductor.org/next/bioc-release/package/drugTargetInteractions.html.
> Any redesign, dashboard-style or otherwise, needs proper community review
> first, and wasn?t something that we wanted as a side effect of the
> migration. I've recorded your suggestion so it's part of that discussion:
> https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/109
>
> Thanks again,
> Sean

On Fri, Oct 9, 2026 at 2:48?PM Thomas Girke <thomas.girke at ucr.edu> wrote:

>

> r-universe failures affect the package?s inclusion? Would it be possible to
> retain the package in the upcoming release based on the existing
> Bioconductor build results?
>

Hi Thomas,

As long as we have an indication that you will rectify the problem as soon
as time permits, package build/check failure at version
transition will not lead to removal from Bioconductor.


> I understand that these issues need to be resolved and I am committed to
> do so. My concern is the timing: faculty workloads vary considerably over
> the academic year, and October is particularly difficult for me to
> accommodate unexpected maintenance work on such short notice. Knowing what
> is required before the release, and what could be addressed afterward,
> would help me prioritize.
>
> Thanks again for your help and for recording the layout suggestion. Your
> example layout looks great.
>
> Best,
>

>> r-universe; this is a weird transition state. When r-universe can't build a
>> package's vignettes, the list comes up empty, even though the vignette is
>> on bioconductor.org. We'll make the pages read vignettes from the same
>> place as everything else. It affects a couple of hundred packages, tracked
>> here:
>>
>> https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-infrastructure/issues/108
>>
>> For drugTargetInteractions there's a real issue underneath. The
>> r-universe build of 1.21.14 fails while building the vignette:

>>   Quitting from drugTargetInteractions.Rmd:564-570 [gtopdb_build]
>>   Error in `.util_download()`: bfcadd() failed

>> https://www.guidetopharmacology.org/services/interactions, and GtoPdb
>> now requires an API key for its web services. Every /services/ endpoint
>> returns 401 "API key is missing". The HGNC mapping file is still public.

>> because the build machines keep BiocFileCache between runs, so

>> without that download or needs an API key: for example a small bundled
>> extract, or skipping the chunk when the download fails.
